EVIDENCE CARD BEFORE PERSISTENCE
Before saving new or updated memory, show a short evidence card. For each observed fact you plan to retain, include a verbatim supporting excerpt and its source locator. Identify whether the excerpt is an initial task claim or an executed observation; do not turn initial task status into a final outcome. Keep only facts those excerpts establish. Omit background, history and wider guarantees that the supplied evidence does not establish, even when you believe them true. If useful transfer remains uncertain, record a question to check in future work instead of asserting that it generalizes.

Inspect this card for unsupported statements before calling bd remember. Persist the checked evidence card itself, including its quotations, locators and uncertainty, rather than replacing it with a broader summary. Preserve the existing inventory and material-novelty checks. If existing memory already covers the supported lesson, leave it unchanged unless the supplied source supports a material correction or useful new evidence; preserve the same existing-key update rule. Verify the persistence acknowledgement before reporting that a write succeeded.

EVIDENCE CHECK BEFORE PERSISTENCE
Before calling bd remember, check each proposed factual claim against a specific passage or executed result in the supplied evidence. Omit claims that have no such support; do not fill gaps from general knowledge. Treat a version range, wider set of locations, or universal recommendation as a separate claim requiring its own evidence. Record unknown scope explicitly. Keep observed facts distinct from a conditional suggestion to verify in a future task. Save only the checked record, and inspect the command result.

BD MEMORY CAPTURE CONTRACT
After reviewing the attached earlier evidence, check existing memory by running exactly:

bd memories --json

Inspect the full returned values before deciding whether the supported reusable lesson is already recorded. An empty phrase search is not evidence of absence. When a materially useful source-supported lesson is absent, persist it with bd remember "<record>" --key "<stable descriptive key>". Replace placeholders with your record and key. When existing memory covers it, leave it unchanged unless the source supports a material correction or useful new evidence; update the existing key for that case rather than duplicating the same lesson under a new key.

The actual stored record must separate: observed environment; exact source evidence/citations; observed failure and the caller recovery/error contract; limits and conditional transfer advice. Only claim environments, versions and behavior established by the supplied evidence. Preserve the source's scope in the stored text itself; do not turn two observed locations into advice for every parser or input boundary. When a limit is unknown, say so. Check the bd command outcome before claiming persistence, and report whether you saved, updated or left memory unchanged and why.

Review the attached historical engineering task and its executed failure/verification excerpts. Explain what was established, its limitations, and any reusable project lesson. This is a review of completed historical work, not a request to rerun or modify that task. Use only the attached earlier evidence for historical claims.

The historical task and verification excerpts are available in PRIOR_TASK.md and PRIOR_SOURCE_PACKET.md in this workspace.
